disagreements.topic: Alternate-function labels for pins 12, 35, 38, 40 in the Fritzing part
disagreements.says_a: pin 12 GPIO 18 (PCM CLK), pin 35 GPIO 19 (PCM FS), pin 38 GPIO 20 (PCM DIN), pin 40 GPIO 21 (PCM DOUT)

disagreements.resolution: Not a conflict on the GPIO numbers: both agree on BCM 18, 19, 20, 21. Fritzing names a different alternate function (PWM0 and SPI1). For the I2S amplifier wiring use the pinout.xyz PCM names. The Fritzing descriptions also misspell Ground as 'Gound' on pins 14, 20, 25.

claims.claim: Vendor product page title is 'Adafruit USB Type C Power Delivery Dummy - I2C or Switchable [HUSB238 - STEMMA QT / Qwiic]'.
claims.note: This is the screw terminal plus DIP switch version. The sibling 'Adafruit USB Type C Power Delivery Dummy Breakout' (5807) uses solder jumpers instead.

claims.claim: The DIP bank has 6 switches selecting 5, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 20 V: switch 6 = 5V, 5 = 9V, 4 = 12V, 3 = 15V, 2 = 18V, 1 = 20V (voltage printed left of each switch, number printed right). Flip ON the switch next to the voltage you need.
claims.note: The parent brief listed 5/9/12/15/20 V; the board also has an 18 V switch.

claims.claim: If no switch is ON, the board requests the highest voltage the charger offers, which can be up to 20 V.
claims.note: For the earlier 20 V design (retired 2026-10-13): all switches OFF still gives only the charger's highest PDO, so a charger without a 20 V PDO will deliver less. Check with a voltmeter.

claims.claim: Schematic: switch 6 shorts the HUSB238 VSET pin to GND; switches 5, 4, 3, 2 connect 6K, 10K, 14K and 18K resistors from VSET to GND; switch 1 is unconnected, so VSET open (all others OFF) means 20 V.
claims.note: HUSB238 datasheet Table 5: 0 ohm 5 V, 6.04K 9 V, 10K 12 V, 14K 15 V, 17.8K 18 V, open 20 V (https://cdn-learn.adafruit.com/assets/assets/000/125/150/original/husb238_datasheet_full.pdf).

claims.claim: With several switches ON the resistors are in parallel: any combination including switch 6 (5V) requests 5 V; other combinations give a resistance below the lowest selected resistor, which maps to a voltage at or below the lowest selected one. Adafruit does not document this case and the datasheet does not define in-between resistances.
claims.note: Inference from the schematic and HUSB238 datasheet Table 5. Practical rule: exactly one switch ON (or all OFF for the highest).

claims.claim: Unplug the USB-C power before changing switches; the board back reads 'Disconnect load before switching voltages! Check with voltmeter to verify!'.
claims.note: Back silkscreen visible in shop photo https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/970x728/5991-01.jpg.

claims.claim: ISet jumper (top right, above the DIP switches) connects to the HUSB238 ISET pin and sets the current the board requests: closed (default) 1.25 A, cut open 3.25 A.
claims.note: Default closed confirmed by the trace visible between the pads in the photo and by HUSB238 datasheet Table 6 (0 ohm 1.25 A, open 3.25 A).

claims.claim: Cutting ISET can stop the board reaching 20 V on chargers whose 20 V PDO offers only 3 A, because the HUSB238 only picks a source PDO whose current is at least the requested current, otherwise it tries the next lower voltage.
claims.note: Inference from the datasheet 'RDO determination' section; not stated by Adafruit. Keep ISet closed unless tested.

claims.claim: The output terminal block has + (selected voltage out) and - (common ground); + is the left screw and - the right screw in this photo.
claims.note: Left/right from the silkscreen plus and minus symbols in the photo.

claims.claim: Two OFF pads below the DIP switches: a switch between them disconnects the internal pass FET (output off) when closed.
Green power LED in the lower left shows the terminal block is powered; cutting the LED jumper above it disables the LED.
USB data lines are broken out to D+ and D- pads to the right of the USB-C port.
claims.note: The D+ and D- labels are printed on the back of the board.

claims.claim: HUSB238 RDO determination: the chip requests the highest source PDO with voltage <= the VSET voltage and current >= the ISET current; if none qualifies at the highest voltage it tries the next lower PDO (default fuse option; the 003DD part marked on the 5991 photo has the 'Next PDO' mismatch action in the ordering guide). So with 15V selected and ISet closed (1.25 A), a charger without a 15 V offer gives its next lower voltage, and with ISet cut (3.25 A) a 15 V / 3 A offer does not qualify.
